title: Stabilizer Rényi moments beyond entanglement
abstract: Stabilizer Rényi moments depend on a choice of operator basis and need not be determined by entanglement spectra. In this paper, we study their spatial decay in critical quantum chains described by two-dimensional conformal field theories. We derive an exact entanglement baseline for reductions of pure stabilizer states and a symmetry selection rule for the charged contribution at fixed support. An exact Ising example shows that an on-site rotation changes the full decay exponent while preserving every subsystem entanglement spectrum. For growing Ising intervals at index two, we obtain an exact Pfaffian representation and compare the charged amplitude with a candidate conformal boundary calculation. The data support this prediction, but its identification with the lattice limit still requires endpoint matching and control of the order of limits.
summary: This paper analyzes Stabilizer Rényi moments in critical quantum chains described by CFTs, showing that these moments provide information beyond standard entanglement measures. The authors derive exact relations and demonstrate that local changes in the Hamiltonian can affect these moments without altering the entanglement spectrum. This work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum correlations in many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the spatial decay of Stabilizer Rényi moments, which are sensitive to the choice of operator basis and do not always correlate directly with entanglement spectra.
main_result: The authors derive an exact entanglement baseline for pure stabilizer states and find that an on-site rotation in the Ising model can alter the decay exponent while preserving the entanglement spectrum.
method: The analysis employs techniques from Conformal Field Theory (CFT) to study the decay of generalized mutual information ($	ext{Istab}_\alpha$) in critical quantum chains, involving cross-ratios and boundary CFT descriptions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on critical quantum chains modeled by two-dimensional CFTs, utilizing stabilizer states (like the Ising model) and analyzing correlation functions in separated regions.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi moments ($Z_\alpha$), generalized mutual information ($	ext{Istab}_\alpha$), and the residual term $A_\alpha(A)$.
important_parameters: The Rényi index $\alpha$, the cross-ratio $\eta$, and the correlation length/separation distance $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping lattice correlations to continuum CFT descriptions, requiring careful control over the order of limits (endpoint matching).
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference equations detailing decay exponents, Pfaffian representations, and boundary CFT forms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the moments and establishing the entanglement baseline, then analyzing the residual terms, deriving symmetry selection rules, and finally applying these concepts to specific models like the Ising chain to derive continuum predictions.
why_interesting: The connection between operator-dependent quantities (Stabilizer moments) and entanglement measures in critical systems provides a powerful, non-standard diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum phases, relevant to understanding correlation functions in strongly correlated materials.
